draft.title: Tourism and the sites
card: Pompeii and Herculaneum attract millions of visitors each year. Pompeii is among the most visited sites in Italy.
Ticket sales and related spending bring in money. This helps pay for excavation, repair and staff, and it creates local jobs.
Visitors wear down the sites. Feet erode paving and thresholds, hands touch walls, and crowds can raise damp. Some visitors take small pieces as souvenirs.
Managers balance the two. They may limit numbers, close fragile houses, set paths and rotate which buildings are open.
draft.remember: Tourism both pays for the sites and wears them down, so managers have to balance the two.

a.q: Which choice shows how tourism helps the sites?
opts: Ticket income can fund repairs and staff
Crowds slow the damage done by weather
Visitors make excavation unnecessary
Souvenir taking keeps the sites tidy
a.why: Money from tickets can pay for conservation work. Crowds do not slow weather damage, and they add wear of their own.
a.clue: Think about where the money for repairs can come from.

b.q: Managers at a site rotate which houses are open and close others for a time. What is the main reason?
opts: To reduce wear on fragile buildings
To raise the price of tickets
To stop weather reaching the walls
To cut the number of visitors to zero
b.why: Rotating access spreads the wear from feet and hands so each house gets time to rest. It does not stop weather, and visitors still come, so income continues.
b.clue: Which cost of tourism does closing a house ease?

a.best: Ticket income can fund repairs and staff

b.best: To reduce wear on fragile buildings

problems.detail: The distractors are implausible for Year 12 HSC students: souvenir taking keeping sites tidy, visitors making excavation unnecessary, crowds slowing weather damage. The clue then points straight to money, the only option about income, so the question can be answered without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The card's facts are accurate and both questions have one clear right answer. Question a is too easy for Year 12, because its distractors are absurd and its clue points directly to the money option.

a.q: Which statement best describes tourism's effect on Pompeii and Herculaneum?
opts: Visitor money funds repairs while visitors add wear
Visitor money funds repairs, so visitors do no harm
Visitors add wear, so tourism gives the sites nothing
Visitors add wear, but their money only funds local jobs
a.why: Ticket money can pay for excavation, repair and staff, yet feet, hands and crowds also wear the sites down. The option saying visitors do no harm ignores this wear, and the option about local jobs ignores the money that goes to repairs.
a.clue: Check the benefit line and the cost line together.

b.q: Managers at a site rotate which houses are open and close others for a time. What is the main reason?
opts: To reduce wear on fragile buildings
To raise the price of tickets
To stop weather reaching the walls
To push visitors towards Herculaneum
b.why: Rotating access spreads the wear from feet and hands so each house gets time to rest. Closed houses are still exposed to weather, and visitors still come to the site, so income continues.
b.clue: Which cost of tourism does closing a house ease?
